title: Workload and Work Stress of Healthcare Professionals in Singapore
what_it_is: Workload and Work Stress of Healthcare Professionals in Singapore

sections.label: Singapore doctor and nurse ratios
sections.summary: Singapore's doctor-to-population ratio of 21 per 10,000 is comparable to Hong Kong and Taiwan, and its 2014 nurse ratio of 69 is comparable to theirs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The doctor to population ratios for Australia, Japan, South Korea, the United Kingdom (UK) and the United States (US) ranged from 22 to 34.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Singapore's doctor-to-population of 21 doctors per 10,000 population is comparable to the ratios of Asian economies like Hong Kong and Taiwan, at 18.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Singapore's ratio in 2014 was 69 nurses per 10,000 population, which is comparable to the ratios of Hong Kong and Taiwan at 66 and 60 respectively.

sections.label: Healthcare facilities for ageing population
sections.summary: MOH is building acute hospitals, community hospitals and nursing homes, and is on track for 9,000 acute, 3,000 community and 17,000 nursing home beds by 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: To prepare for an ageing population, the Ministry of Health (MOH) has been building more healthcare facilities, such as acute hospitals, community hospitals and nursing homes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: We are on track to meet our target of providing 9,000 acute beds, 3,000 community hospital beds and 17,000 nursing home beds by 2020.

sections.label: Hospital job satisfaction and infection control
sections.summary: Seven of eight hospitals had higher or comparable job satisfaction scores than the national norm, and workload was not a direct cause of infections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: In the latest survey, seven out of eight of our hospitals have either higher or comparable job satisfaction scores, compared to the Singapore national norm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I think the suggestion from Mr Perera about looking at how we can further improve the work environment for our healthcare professionals is something we will certainly consider.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We are looking at not just the work environment for our healthcare workers, but also how we can use the opportunity to improve productivity which will lead to better quality of care, better service for our patients and also to look at whether we can reduce the manpower requirements for our healthcare sector to be ready for an ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: These are ideas which we will take a look at, in our continuous effort to try and improve productivity and sustainability of our healthcare system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I also want to take the opportunity to assure Mr Perera that we are doing a thorough review on how to improve infection control and also to look at the detection and response to outbreaks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The investigations that were done by the various hospitals and the professionals indicate that workload has not been a direct cause of these infections.
